name: vix_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when India VIX surges >4% within 10 minutes, it reflects panic-driven put buying that temporarily dislocates implied volatility above fair value. The precise entry trigger is the moment VIX stops making new highs (3 consecutive declining 5-second bars) — this signals put-buying saturation. At that inflection point, option market makers who sold the panic puts begin aggressive NIFTY futures purchases to delta-hedge their short-gamma exposure, generating a 10-25 spot-point mean-reversion bounce within 30-90 seconds. The complementary short signal fires when VIX is crushed >3% in 10 minutes at NIFTY highs — complacency at elevated levels where the same MMs delta-hedge the opposite direction as volatility re-prices up.

indicators.name: vix_change_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute VIX percentage change. Original used 30-min (360 1-min bars) but at 5-second resolution we hold only 30-120 seconds, so we need the FAST panic signal. A 10-min spike is already large enough to signal genuine panic selling — 30-min would be too slow to enter at the right moment for a 90-second trade.

indicators.name: vix_zscore_360
indicators.purpose: 30-minute rolling VIX z-score for intraday context. Original used 20-day SMA (7500 1-min bars) which captures structural VIX regime but changes too slowly for intraday signals. We use 30-min (360 5s bars) to detect elevation vs the current session's baseline — this is the relevant context for whether today's spike is anomalous or part of an already-elevated day.

indicators.name: vix_declining_3
indicators.formula: vix_close[t] < vix_close[t-1] AND vix_close[t-1] < vix_close[t-2] AND vix_close[t-2] < vix_close[t-3]
indicators.purpose: 3 consecutive declining VIX bars (15 seconds of deceleration). This is the precise entry trigger copied directly from the original's '3 consecutive declining bars' confirmation — at 5-second resolution this is the earliest detectable sign that put-buying pressure is exhausting and MM delta-hedging is beginning. Cannot use fewer bars (too noisy at 5s).

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute RSI to confirm NIFTY oversold condition at entry. Original used RSI(14) on 1-min bars = 14 minutes of signal. We compress to RSI(36) = 3 min at 5-second bars because we are entering for a 30-90 second bounce and need RSI to reflect the CURRENT fast dip, not the 14-minute average. A 3-min oversold condition aligns with the 10-min VIX spike lookback.

conditions: vix_change_120 > vix_spike_threshold (VIX spiked >4% in last 10 minutes)
vix_zscore_360 > 1.0 (VIX is elevated vs 30-min session baseline)
vix_declining_3 == True (VIX has decelerated for 3 consecutive 5s bars)
rsi_36 < rsi_oversold (NIFTY oversold on 3-min RSI, default 35)
buy_ce.confirmation: All 4 conditions must be True simultaneously. vix_declining_3 is the timing pin — it fires only at the VIX top, not during the spike itself.

conditions: vix_change_120 < -vix_crush_threshold (VIX crushed >3% in last 10 minutes — complacency)
vix_rising_3 == True (VIX has started rising for 3 consecutive 5s bars)
rsi_36 > rsi_overbought (NIFTY overbought on 3-min RSI, default 65)
buy_pe.confirmation: Complacency reversal: VIX bottomed and started rising while NIFTY is at short-term highs.

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. If NIFTY moves 8 pts further against us after VIX 'tops out', the deceleration signal was false and the spike is continuing — the mean-reversion thesis is wrong. NIFTY 30s typical move is 2-5 option pts; 4 pts is one standard deviation beyond expected noise.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. VIX mean-reversion bounces on NIFTY average 15-25 spot points in the first 60-90 seconds post-deceleration. Targeting 14 spot pts captures ~65% of the median first-leg recovery with a 1:1.75 risk-reward ratio.
exit.eod_rule: flatten at 14:00 IST — VIX spikes after 14:00 have insufficient session time to revert

filters.vix_filter: Core signal — requires 10-min VIX spike >4% AND vix_zscore > 1.0 for genuine dislocation
filters.time_filter: 09:20-14:00 IST only. Original explicitly noted post-14:00 spikes are less likely to revert within session; we enforce this as a hard filter.
filters.volume_filter: None applied directly — VIX itself is volume-weighted by definition
filters.trend_filter: vix_zscore_360 > 1.0 ensures spike is elevated vs current session, not just noise
filters.spread_filter: N/A — limit order execution at candle close; no bid-ask spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VIX mean-reversion is structural (option market-maker gamma hedging) and persists across global markets. The MM delta-hedging mechanism is mechanical, not behavioural.

adaptation_notes: Three major changes from original: (1) VIX spike window compressed from 30-min to 10-min (120 5s bars) to match 30-120s hold time — we trade the FAST reversal, not the slow recovery. (2) VIX z-score shifted from 20-day to 30-min rolling window — intraday baseline is more relevant for same-session reversion thesis. (3) Session cutoff enforced at 14:00 IST (original noted this preference but treated as soft filter; we make it hard). RSI(36) = 3-min retained exactly from original's 14-min RSI logic compressed proportionally to match our hold time.
weaknesses: VIX spike frequency at 10-min window is low (3-5 qualifying signals per week on NIFTY), making this capital-inefficient as a standalone strategy — must be combined
The VIX-declining-3-bars confirmation adds 15 seconds of lag; on fast spike-and-reverse days, the bounce may be 50% done before entry
During genuine crises (global macro shock, RBI surprise), the VIX spike does NOT revert intraday and the strategy takes the full stop loss
vix_zscore_360 uses only 30 minutes of session history; in the first 30 minutes of trading, the z-score is unreliable — signal quality is lower in the opening period

_source.original_stop: VIX makes new session high OR NIFTY drops another 0.5%
_source.original_target: VIX reverts 50% of spike OR NIFTY recovers 50% of drawdown
